outcome: Detect, prioritise and review harmful text, voice, names and behaviour with full context and a working appeal route — while every sanction stays a human decision
overview: Multilingual chat, voice and username volume outpaces any moderation team, while context-free automation issues unfair sanctions that communities never forgive. This solution classifies and prioritises reported and detected harm across Arabic and English, gives reviewers the surrounding context and the policy clause that applies, and leaves every sanction and appeal decision with the customer’s own trained moderators. Child-safety signals follow stricter routing, minimum retention and separate handling by design. An 8–12-week benchmark and pilot measures time to review severe reports, precision and recall at approved thresholds, and reviewer wellbeing alongside throughput. Reference builds are specified for AWS and Azure, with Gulf data residency for regional publishers.

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); reported content, evidence and reviewer decisions remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, under minimum-retention rules

notFor.situation: No written community policy or harm taxonomy
notFor.why: Classification can only enforce a policy that exists; without a taxonomy there is nothing to be precise or fair about, and thresholds cannot be approved

notFor.situation: No trained human moderators to decide sanctions and appeals
notFor.why: The solution prioritises and evidences; it never issues sanctions automatically, so without reviewers the queue simply grows

notFor.situation: Child-directed platforms without a child-safety and legal function in place
notFor.why: Minors’ data, reporting duties and law-enforcement boundaries need named accountable owners before any detection tooling is introduced
